summary: Shin'ichi Yoshinaga was a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1976 to 1983 and held a post at the National Institute of Technology, Maizuru College, from around 1990 to 2018.
Shin'ichiro Hori works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held positions at the University of Tokyo and at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, where he served as Acting Director.

Shindai Sekiguchi specialized in Buddhist studies, graduating from Taisho University around 1931. He served as a professor at Taisho University from circa 1961 to 1978 and at Hanazono University from circa 1978 to 1982.

Shingen Takagi worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, Hakuyu Hadano, Yusho Miyasaka, and Gisho Nakano, later earning a PhD from Rissho University. He served as president of Koyasan University (circa 1968–2003).

Shingo Einoo is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Wilhelm Rau between 1974 and 1979. He worked at the National Museum of Ethnology (circa 1980–1986) and as a professor at the University of Tokyo (circa 1999–2013).

Shinichi Tsuda is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and earned his PhD at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Arthur Llewellyn Basham, later teaching at ICPBS.

Shinjo Kawasaki works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Supervised by Hajime Nakamura at the University of Tokyo, he held posts at Toyo Bunko, the University of Tsukuba from 1975, and Taisho University from circa 2004 to 2008.

Shinjo Suguro specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1948 to 1987, receiving a doctorate, and served as vice director at Rissho University in 1980.
Shinkai Sugawara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University from circa 1948 to 1954 and later held a post there from circa 1971 to 1996.

Shinkan Murakami studied Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy at Tohoku University (circa 1952–1979) under Ensho Kanakura, Ryujo Yamada, Hakuyu Hadano, and Nobuo Kumagai. He served in the Faculty of Arts and Letters at Tohoku University and at Seiwa Gakuen College.

Shinko Mochizuki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bukkyo University under Togai Soga and Tokuo Jobon. He served as head of Shukyo University (1908–1928) and Taisho University (1926–1942), and held posts at Waseda, Tendai Sect University, and Chion-in.

Shinobu Arai Apple is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey, committee member Hiroshi Kanno, teacher Mark Csikszentmihalyi, and academic adviser Robert Bickner.
Shinobu Yamaguchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned a PhD from Nagoya University around 1990–1995 and serves as a professor at Toyo University.

Shinsho Hanayama was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (circa 1918–1921). He held positions at Toyo University (circa 1923–1934), Kokugakuin University, and taught Buddhism at the University of Tokyo (circa 1934–1959).

Shinshu Kusumoto is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Hiroshima University (circa 1996–2001) under doctoral supervisor Shoryu Katsura. He also studied under Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.

Shintaro Kitano is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under the supervision of Kazunobu Matsuda. Kitano has held positions as a researcher at Taisho University and as a lecturer at Kyushu University.
Shinten Sakai was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Shindo Shiraishi and held a post at Koyasan University from circa 1952 to 1982.

Shinya Moriyama specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed master's studies at the University of Tokyo, earned a Dr.Phil at the University of Vienna, where he studied under Eli Franco, and took up a teaching post at Shinshu University around 2013.
Shinya Yasutomi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University from circa 1963 to 1967. He served as a professor at Otani University from circa 1996 to 2010.

Shiro Matsumoto is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Yasuaki Nara and Zuiho Yamaguchi. He became a professor at Komazawa University and was a visiting professor at the University of Chicago.
